Content: import request from 'supertest';
import app from '../../src/app';
import { prisma } from '../../src/config/prisma';
import { getAuthToken } from '../helpers/authHelpers';

const validVehicle = {
  make: 'Toyota',
  model: 'Corolla',
  category: 'Sedan',
  price: 20000,
  quantity: 5,
};

/** Seeds a vehicle directly through Prisma to arrange a scenario. */
const seedVehicle = async (overrides: Partial<typeof validVehicle> = {}) =>
  prisma.vehicle.create({ data: { ...validVehicle, ...overrides } });

describe('POST /api/vehicles', () => {
  it('responds 201 with the created vehicle for an ADMIN', async () => {
    // Arrange
    const token = await getAuthToken('ADMIN');

    // Act
    const response = await request(app)
      .post('/api/vehicles')
      .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`)
      .send(validVehicle);

    // Assert
    expect(response.status).toBe(201);
    expect(response.body).toEqual({
      id: expect.any(Number),
      make: validVehicle.make,
      model: validVehicle.model,
      category: validVehicle.category,
      price: validVehicle.price,
      quantity: validVehicle.quantity,
      createdAt: expect.any(String),
      updatedAt: expect.any(String),
    });
  });

  it('responds 400 when the body is invalid', async () => {
    // Arrange
    const token = await getAuthToken('ADMIN');
    const invalidBody = { make: '', model: 'Corolla', category: 'Sedan', price: -1 };

    // Act
    const response = await request(app)
      .post('/api/vehicles')
      .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`)
      .send(invalidBody);

    // Assert
    expect(response.status).toBe(400);
    expect(response.body).toHaveProperty('error');
    expect(typeof response.body.error.message).toBe('string');
  });

  it('responds 403 for a USER', async () => {
    // Arrange
    const token = await getAuthToken('USER');

    // Act
    const response = await request(app)
      .post('/api/vehicles')
      .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`)
      .send(validVehicle);

    // Assert
    expect(response.status).toBe(403);
    expect(response.body).toHaveProperty('error');
  });

  it('responds 401 without a token', async () => {
    // Act
    const response = await request(app).post('/api/vehicles').send(validVehicle);

    // Assert
    expect(response.status).toBe(401);
    expect(response.body).toHaveProperty('error');
  });
});

Path: backend/tests/integration/inventory.test.ts
Content: import request from 'supertest';
import app from '../../src/app';
import { prisma } from '../../src/config/prisma';
import { getAuthToken } from '../helpers/authHelpers';

const validVehicle = {
  make: 'Toyota',
  model: 'Corolla',
  category: 'Sedan',
  price: 20000,
  quantity: 5,
};

/** Seeds a vehicle directly through Prisma to arrange a scenario. */
const seedVehicle = async (overrides: Partial<typeof validVehicle> = {}) =>
  prisma.vehicle.create({ data: { ...validVehicle, ...overrides } });

describe('Inventory: purchase', () => {
  it('decrements stock by exactly 1', async () => {
    // Arrange
    const token = await getAuthToken('USER');
    const vehicle = await seedVehicle({ quantity: 5 });

    // Act
    const response = await request(app)
      .post(`/api/vehicles/${vehicle.id}/purchase`)
      .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`);

    // Assert
    expect(response.status).toBe(200);
    expect(response.body.quantity).toBe(4);
    const stored = await prisma.vehicle.findUnique({ where: { id: vehicle.id } });
    expect(stored?.quantity).toBe(4);
  });

  it('returns 409 and leaves stock at 0 when purchasing an out-of-stock vehicle', async () => {
    // Arrange
    const token = await getAuthToken('USER');
    const vehicle = await seedVehicle({ quantity: 0 });

    // Act
    const response = await request(app)
      .post(`/api/vehicles/${vehicle.id}/purchase`)
      .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`);

    // Assert
    expect(response.status).toBe(409);
    expect(response.body).toHaveProperty('error');
    const stored = await prisma.vehicle.findUnique({ where: { id: vehicle.id } });
    expect(stored?.quantity).toBe(0);
  });
});

describe('Inventory: restock', () => {
  it('increases stock by the requested amount', async () => {
    // Arrange
    const token = await getAuthToken('ADMIN');
    const vehicle = await seedVehicle({ quantity: 2 });

    // Act
    const response = await request(app)
      .post(`/api/vehicles/${vehicle.id}/restock`)
      .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`)
      .send({ quantity: 8 });

    // Assert
    expect(response.status).toBe(200);
    expect(response.body.quantity).toBe(10);
    const stored = await prisma.vehicle.findUnique({ where: { id: vehicle.id } });
    expect(stored?.quantity).toBe(10);
  });

  it('restocks an out-of-stock vehicle back to a positive quantity', async () => {
    // Arrange
    const token = await getAuthToken('ADMIN');
    const vehicle = await seedVehicle({ quantity: 0 });

    // Act
    const response = await request(app)
      .post(`/api/vehicles/${vehicle.id}/restock`)
      .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`)
      .send({ quantity: 3 });

    // Assert
    expect(response.status).toBe(200);
    expect(response.body.quantity).toBe(3);
  });
});

describe('Inventory: concurrency', () => {
  it('allows exactly one of two simultaneous purchases when only one unit is in stock', async () => {
    // Arrange
    const token = await getAuthToken('USER');
    const vehicle = await seedVehicle({ quantity: 1 });

    // Act
    const [first, second] = await Promise.all([
      request(app)
        .post(`/api/vehicles/${vehicle.id}/purchase`)
        .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`),
      request(app)
        .post(`/api/vehicles/${vehicle.id}/purchase`)
        .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`),
    ]);

    // Assert
    const statuses = [first.status, second.status].sort();
    expect(statuses).toEqual([200, 409]);
    const stored = await prisma.vehicle.findUnique({ where: { id: vehicle.id } });
    expect(stored?.quantity).toBe(0);
  });
});

Result: TDD RED phase complete. I wrote three new test files and touched nothing under `backend/src`.

## Files created

- [`tests/unit/vehicleService.test.ts`](backend/tests/unit/vehicleService.test.ts) — mocks `VehicleRepository` via `jest.mock`, injects it into `VehicleService`, and covers every method: `addVehicle` (incl. quantity defaulting to 0), `listVehicles` (includes quantity-0), `searchVehicles` (forwards filters, 400 when `minPrice > maxPrice`, allows equal bounds), `updateVehicle` (200 + 404), `deleteVehicle` (200 + 404), `purchaseVehicle` (decrement, 404, 409 `"Out of stock"`), `restockVehicle` (increase, 404, 400 for non-positive amount).
- [`tests/integration/vehicles.test.ts`](backend/tests/integration/vehicles.test.ts) — supertest against the real app + test DB using [`getAuthToken`](backend/tests/helpers/authHelpers.ts:45). Covers all 7 routes, every status code (201/200/204/400/401/403/404/409), the 401 case for each route, USER vs ADMIN permissions, each search filter individually (make/model partial case-insensitive, category case-insensitive, inclusive price range), combined filters, the `minPrice > maxPrice` and non-numeric price 400s, the `/search`-not-shadowed-by-`/:id` case, and quantity-0 vehicles still appearing in the list.
- [`tests/integration/inventory.test.ts`](backend/tests/integration/inventory.test.ts) — purchase decrements by exactly 1 (verified in DB), purchase at 0 → 409 with stock staying 0, restock increases correctly (incl. from 0), and the concurrency test: quantity 1 + two `Promise.all` purchases → statuses `[200, 409]` and final quantity 0.

All tests use arrange/act/assert, unique emails (via the helper's random suffix), and rely on the existing `beforeEach` DB reset — no shared mutable state.

**All 26 existing tests pass.** The 41 new failures are exclusively:
- `vehicleService.test.ts`: `Cannot find module '../../src/repositories/vehicleRepository'` (suite can't run — module doesn't exist).
- `vehicles.test.ts` / `inventory.test.ts`: assertion failures where routes return `404` (routes not mounted yet).

I grepped the full output for `SyntaxError`, `TypeError`, and `ReferenceError` — none present, so the failures are purely missing modules/routes.

## Note on the parallel-run flake

The two auth failures under plain `npm test` are **not** caused by my tests. All integration suites share one SQLite file (`DATABASE_URL="file:./test.db"` in [`backend/.env.test`](backend/.env.test:1)) and Jest runs suites in parallel workers, so [`resetDb.ts`](backend/tests/setup/resetDb.ts:7)'s `deleteMany()` in one worker wipes rows another worker is mid-test on. This is a pre-existing infrastructure limitation that only surfaced now because there are more DB-touching suites. I left it untouched since it's outside this task's scope; the fix (when you want it) is either `--runInBand`/`maxWorkers: 1` in [`jest.config.js`](backend/jest.config.js:1) or a per-worker database file.

<user_message>
TDD GREEN phase for vehicles and inventory. The failing tests already exist in /backend/tests. Implement the minimum production code under /backend/src to make ALL tests pass. Do not weaken, delete or edit any test. If you believe a test is wrong, STOP and tell me why instead of changing it.

Create, following the existing auth code as the style reference:
1. src/repositories/vehicleRepository.ts: VehicleRepository with create, findAll, findById, search, update, delete, decrementStockIfAvailable, increaseStock, using the shared Prisma client.
   - decrementStockIfAvailable must be atomic: use prisma.vehicle.updateMany({ where: { id, quantity: { gt: 0 } }, data: { quantity: { decrement: 1 } } }). If count is 0 return null, otherwise return the updated vehicle. Never read-then-write.
   - SQLite note: do NOT use Prisma's mode: 'insensitive', the SQLite connector rejects it. Prisma's contains is already case-insensitive for ASCII on SQLite, so use contains for make and model. For category, apply the other filters in the database and then filter category case-insensitively in memory (compare lowercased values).
   - Price range is inclusive (gte and lte).
2. src/services/vehicleService.ts: VehicleService(vehicleRepository) with addVehicle, listVehicles, searchVehicles, updateVehicle, deleteVehicle, purchaseVehicle, restockVehicle. Errors use AppError: 404 for a missing vehicle, 409 "Out of stock" on purchase at quantity 0 (an existing vehicle with no stock), 400 for minPrice greater than maxPrice, 400 for non-positive restock amounts.
3. Zod schemas in src/utils/validation.ts: create vehicle (make, model, category non-empty trimmed strings, price > 0, quantity integer >= 0 default 0), partial update (at least one field), search query (optional strings, optional numeric minPrice and maxPrice, reject non-numeric), restock body ({ quantity: positive integer }), and an id param schema (positive integer, reject anything else with 400).
4. src/controllers/vehicleController.ts: thin handlers, no business logic. DELETE responds 204 with no body.
5. src/routes/vehicleRoutes.ts wired as VehicleRepository -> VehicleService -> VehicleController. Apply authenticate to every route. Apply requireRole('ADMIN') to POST /, PUT /:id, DELETE /:id and POST /:id/restock. Register GET /search BEFORE any /:id route so it is not shadowed. Mount the router in src/app.ts at /api/vehicles.
6. Keep every error response in the existing { error: { message } } shape.

Constraints: layered architecture, dependency injection through constructors, short functions, JSDoc on public functions, strict TypeScript.

When done run npm test, npm run build and npm run lint and show me the results. If the concurrency test fails with a 500 or a "database is locked" error, report it to me instead of working around it. Do not run git commit.
</user_message>

 6 | const BCRYPT_ROUNDS = 10;
 7 | const DEFAULT_ROLE = 'USER';
 8 | const INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MESSAGE = 'Invalid credentials';
 9 | 
10 | /** Public user shape returned to clients (never includes the password hash). */
11 | export interface PublicUser {
12 |   id: number;
13 |   email: string;
14 |   role: string;

21 | }

23 | /**
24 |  * Authentication business logic: registration and login.
25 |  * Dependencies are injected to keep the service testable and decoupled.
26 |  */
27 | export class AuthService {
28 |   constructor(private readonly userRepository: UserRepository) {}
29 | 
30 |   /**
31 |    * Registers a new user with the USER role and a hashed password.
32 |    *
33 |    * @param email Unique email address.
34 |    * @param password Plaintext password to hash.
35 |    * @returns The created user's public fields.
36 |    * @throws {AppError} 409 when the email is already registered.
37 |    */
38 |   async register(email: string, password: string): Promise<PublicUser> {
39 |     const existing = await this.userRepository.findByEmail(email);
40 |     if (existing) {
41 |       throw new AppError(409, 'Email is already registered');
42 |     }
43 | 
44 |     const passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash(password, BCRYPT_ROUNDS);
45 |     const user = await this.userRepository.create({
46 |       email,
47 |       passwordHash,
48 |       role: DEFAULT_ROLE,
49 |     });
50 | 
51 |     return this.toPublicUser(user);
52 |   }
53 | 
54 |   /**
55 |    * Authenticates a user and issues a signed JWT.
56 |    *
57 |    * @param email Email address.
58 |    * @param password Plaintext password to verify.
59 |    * @returns A signed token and the user's public fields.
60 |    * @throws {AppError} 401 for an unknown email or a wrong password.
61 |    */
62 |   async login(email: string, password: string): Promise<LoginResult> {
63 |     const user = await this.userRepository.findByEmail(email);
64 |     if (!user) {
65 |       throw new AppError(401, INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MESSAGE);
66 |     }
67 | 
68 |     const passwordMatches = await bcrypt.compare(password, user.passwordHash);
69 |     if (!passwordMatches) {
70 |       throw new AppError(401, INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MESSAGE);
71 |     }
72 | 
73 |     return { token: this.signToken(user), user: this.toPublicUser(user) };
74 |   }
75 | 
76 |   /**
77 |    * Signs a JWT for the user. Env vars are read at call time so tests can set them.
78 |    */
79 |   private signToken(user: { id: number; role: string }): string {
80 |     const secret = process.env.JWT_SECRET;
81 |     if (!secret) {
82 |       throw new AppError(500, 'Authentication is not configured');
83 |     }
84 | 
85 |     const options: SignOptions = {
86 |       expiresIn: (process.env.JWT_EXPIRES_IN ?? '1d') as SignOptions['expiresIn'],
87 |     };
88 | 
89 |     return jwt.sign({ sub: String(user.id), role: user.role }, secret, options);
90 |   }
91 | 
92 |   /** Strips sensitive fields from a user record. */
93 |   private toPublicUser(user: { id: number; email: string; role: string }): PublicUser {
94 |     return { id: user.id, email: user.email, role: user.role };
95 |   }
96 | }

 5 | /**
 6 |  * Thin HTTP layer for authentication.

 9 | export class AuthController {
10 |   constructor(private readonly authService: AuthService) {}
11 | 
12 |   /**
13 |    * Handles POST /api/auth/register.
14 |    * Responds 201 with the created user's public fields.
15 |    */

17 |     try {
18 |       const { email, password } = registerSchema.parse(req.body);
19 |       const user = await this.authService.register(email, password);
20 |       res.status(201).json(user);
21 |     } catch (error) {
22 |       next(error);
23 |     }
24 |   };
25 | 
26 |   /**
27 |    * Handles POST /api/auth/login.
28 |    * Responds 200 with a token and the user's public fields.
29 |    */
30 |   login = async (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): Promise<void> => {
31 |     try {
32 |       const { email, password } = loginSchema.parse(req.body);
33 |       const result = await this.authService.login(email, password);
34 |       res.status(200).json(result);
35 |     } catch (error) {
36 |       next(error);

38 |   };
39 | }

23 | export async function createUser(

26 | ): Promise<CreatedUser> {

28 |   const password = overrides.password ?? DEFAULT_PASSWORD;
29 |   const passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash(password, BCRYPT_ROUNDS);

31 |   const user = await prisma.user.create({

33 |   });

36 | }

38 | /**
39 |  * Creates a user with the given role and returns a signed JWT for it.
40 |  * The token mirrors the payload the auth service is expected to produce.
41 |  *

43 |  * @returns A signed JWT string.
44 |  */
45 | export async function getAuthToken(role = 'USER'): Promise<string> {
46 |   const user = await createUser(role);
47 |

50 |   };
51 |

53 |     { sub: String(user.id), role: user.role },
54 |     process.env.JWT_SECRET as string,

 5 | const GENERIC_MESSAGE = 'Internal Server Error';

 7 | /** Builds a Zod error message from the first issue, prefixed by its field path. */
 8 | function formatZodError(error: ZodError): string {
 9 |   const issue = error.issues[0];
10 |   if (!issue) {
11 |     return 'Invalid request payload';
12 |   }
13 |   const field = issue.path.join('.');
14 |   return field ? `${field}: ${issue.message}` : issue.message;
15 | }
16 | 
17 | /**
18 |  * Central error-handling middleware.
19 |  * Every response is JSON shaped as `{ error: { message } }`.
20 |  * Must be registered last, after all routes.
21 |  */
22 | export function errorHandler(
23 |   err: unknown,
24 |   _req: Request,
25 |   res: Response,
26 |   _next: NextFunction,
27 | ): void {
28 |   if (err instanceof AppError) {
29 |     res.status(err.statusCode).json({ error: { message: err.message } });
30 |     return;
31 |   }
32 | 
33 |   if (err instanceof ZodError) {
34 |     res.status(400).json({ error: { message: formatZodError(err) } });
35 |     return;
36 |   }
37 | 
38 |   res.status(500).json({ error: { message: GENERIC_MESSAGE } });
39 | }

 4 | const BEARER_PREFIX = 'Bearer ';
 5 | 
 6 | /**
 7 |  * Verifies the Bearer JWT and attaches `{ id, role }` to `req.user`.
 8 |  * Responds 401 for a missing, malformed, invalid or expired token.
 9 |  */
10 | export function authenticate(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void {
11 |   const header = req.headers.authorization;
12 |   if (!header || !header.startsWith(BEARER_PREFIX)) {
13 |     res.status(401).json({ error: { message: 'Authentication required' } });
14 |     return;
15 |   }
16 | 
17 |   const token = header.slice(BEARER_PREFIX.length).trim();
18 |   const secret = process.env.JWT_SECRET;
19 |   if (!token || !secret) {
20 |     res.status(401).json({ error: { message: 'Invalid or expired token' } });
21 |     return;
22 |   }
23 | 
24 |   try {
25 |     const decoded = jwt.verify(token, secret) as JwtPayload;
26 |     const id = Number(decoded.sub);
27 |     if (!Number.isInteger(id) || typeof decoded.role !== 'string') {
28 |       res.status(401).json({ error: { message: 'Invalid or expired token' } });
29 |       return;
30 |     }
31 | 
32 |     req.user = { id, role: decoded.role };
33 |     next();
34 |   } catch {
35 |     res.status(401).json({ error: { message: 'Invalid or expired token' } });
36 |   }
37 | }
38 | 
39 | export default authenticate;

const email = z.string().trim().email('A valid email address is required');
const password = z.string().min(8, 'Password must be at least 8 characters long');

/** Schema for the registration payload. */
export const registerSchema = z.object({ email, password });

/** Schema for the login payload. */
export const loginSchema = z.object({ email, password });

export type RegisterInput = z.infer<typeof registerSchema>;
export type LoginInput = z.infer<typeof loginSchema>;

/** Builds a required, trimmed, non-empty string schema for a named field. */
const requiredText = (field: string) => z.string().trim().min(1, `${field} is required`);

const price = z.number().positive('Price must be greater than 0');
const quantity = z
  .number()
  .int('Quantity must be an integer')
  .min(0, 'Quantity cannot be negative');

/** Schema for creating a vehicle. Quantity defaults to 0 when omitted. */
export const createVehicleSchema = z.object({
  make: requiredText('Make'),
  model: requiredText('Model'),
  category: requiredText('Category'),
  price,
  quantity: quantity.default(0),
});

/** Schema for a partial vehicle update; at least one field must be present. */
export const updateVehicleSchema = z
  .object({
    make: requiredText('Make').optional(),
    model: requiredText('Model').optional(),
    category: requiredText('Category').optional(),
    price: price.optional(),
    quantity: quantity.optional(),
  })
  .refine((data) => Object.keys(data).length > 0, {
    message: 'At least one field must be provided',
  });

/** Schema for the vehicle search query string. Prices are coerced and must be numeric. */
export const searchVehiclesQuerySchema = z.object({
  make: requiredText('Make').optional(),
  model: requiredText('Model').optional(),
  category: requiredText('Category').optional(),
  minPrice: z.coerce.number({ message: 'minPrice must be a number' }).optional(),
  maxPrice: z.coerce.number({ message: 'maxPrice must be a number' }).optional(),
});

/** Schema for the restock payload; the amount must be a positive integer. */
export const restockVehicleSchema = z.object({
  quantity: z
    .number()
    .int('Quantity must be an integer')
    .positive('Quantity must be greater than 0'),
});

/** Schema for a positive integer vehicle id route parameter. */
export const vehicleIdParamSchema = z.object({
  id: z.coerce
    .number({ message: 'Vehicle id must be a number' })
    .int('Vehicle id must be an integer')
    .positive('Vehicle id must be positive'),
});

export type CreateVehicleInput = z.infer<typeof createVehicleSchema>;
export type UpdateVehicleInput = z.infer<typeof updateVehicleSchema>;
export type SearchVehiclesQuery = z.infer<typeof searchVehiclesQuerySchema>;
export type RestockVehicleInput = z.infer<typeof restockVehicleSchema>;

Path: backend/src/repositories/vehicleRepository.ts
Content: import type { Prisma, Vehicle } from '@prisma/client';
import { prisma } from '../config/prisma';

/** Data required to persist a new vehicle. */
export interface CreateVehicleData {
  make: string;
  model: string;
  category: string;
  price: number;
  quantity: number;
}

/** Fields that may be changed on an existing vehicle. */
export type UpdateVehicleData = Partial<CreateVehicleData>;

/** Filters accepted by the vehicle search. */
export interface VehicleSearchFilters {
  make?: string;
  model?: string;
  category?: string;
  minPrice?: number;
  maxPrice?: number;
}

/**
 * Data-access layer for vehicles.
 * Encapsulates all Prisma queries so services stay persistence-agnostic.
 */
export class VehicleRepository {
  /**
   * Persists a new vehicle.
   *
   * @param data Vehicle fields to store.
   * @returns The created vehicle record.
   */
  async create(data: CreateVehicleData): Promise<Vehicle> {
    return prisma.vehicle.create({ data });
  }

  /**
   * Lists every vehicle, including out-of-stock ones.
   *
   * @returns All vehicle records.
   */
  async findAll(): Promise<Vehicle[]> {
    return prisma.vehicle.findMany();
  }

  /**
   * Finds a vehicle by its id.
   *
   * @param id Vehicle identifier.
   * @returns The matching vehicle, or null when none exists.
   */
  async findById(id: number): Promise<Vehicle | null> {
    return prisma.vehicle.findUnique({ where: { id } });
  }

  /**
   * Searches vehicles by optional filters.
   * Make and model use case-insensitive `contains`; category is matched
   * case-insensitively in memory because SQLite rejects Prisma's `mode` option.
   *
   * @param filters Optional make, model, category and inclusive price range.
   * @returns Matching vehicle records.
   */
  async search(filters: VehicleSearchFilters): Promise<Vehicle[]> {
    const where: Prisma.VehicleWhereInput = {};

    if (filters.make) {
      where.make = { contains: filters.make };
    }
    if (filters.model) {
      where.model = { contains: filters.model };
    }
    if (filters.minPrice !== undefined || filters.maxPrice !== undefined) {
      where.price = { gte: filters.minPrice, lte: filters.maxPrice };
    }

    const vehicles = await prisma.vehicle.findMany({ where });
    return this.filterByCategory(vehicles, filters.category);
  }

  /**
   * Updates an existing vehicle.
   *
   * @param id Vehicle identifier.
   * @param data Fields to change.
   * @returns The updated vehicle record.
   */
  async update(id: number, data: UpdateVehicleData): Promise<Vehicle> {
    return prisma.vehicle.update({ where: { id }, data });
  }

  /**
   * Deletes a vehicle.
   *
   * @param id Vehicle identifier.
   * @returns The deleted vehicle record.
   */
  async delete(id: number): Promise<Vehicle> {
    return prisma.vehicle.delete({ where: { id } });
  }

  /**
   * Atomically decrements stock by one when at least one unit is available.
   * Uses a conditional `updateMany` so concurrent purchases cannot oversell.
   *
   * @param id Vehicle identifier.
   * @returns The updated vehicle, or null when it is missing or out of stock.
   */
  async decrementStockIfAvailable(id: number): Promise<Vehicle | null> {
    const { count } = await prisma.vehicle.updateMany({
      where: { id, quantity: { gt: 0 } },
      data: { quantity: { decrement: 1 } },
    });

    if (count === 0) {
      return null;
    }

    return prisma.vehicle.findUnique({ where: { id } });
  }

  /**
   * Atomically increases stock by the given amount.
   *
   * @param id Vehicle identifier.
   * @param amount Positive number of units to add.
   * @returns The updated vehicle record.
   */
  async increaseStock(id: number, amount: number): Promise<Vehicle> {
    return prisma.vehicle.update({
      where: { id },
      data: { quantity: { increment: amount } },
    });
  }

  /** Filters vehicles by category using a case-insensitive comparison. */
  private filterByCategory(vehicles: Vehicle[], category?: string): Vehicle[] {
    if (!category) {
      return vehicles;
    }

    const target = category.toLowerCase();
    return vehicles.filter((vehicle) => vehicle.category.toLowerCase() === target);
  }
}

export default VehicleRepository;

Path: backend/src/services/vehicleService.ts
Content: import type { Vehicle } from '@prisma/client';
import type {
  CreateVehicleData,
  UpdateVehicleData,
  VehicleRepository,
  VehicleSearchFilters,
} from '../repositories/vehicleRepository';
import { AppError } from '../utils/AppError';

const VEHICLE_NOT_FOUND_MESSAGE = 'Vehicle not found';
const OUT_OF_STOCK_MESSAGE = 'Out of stock';

/**
 * Vehicle business logic: catalogue management and inventory operations.
 * Dependencies are injected to keep the service testable and decoupled.
 */
export class VehicleService {
  constructor(private readonly vehicleRepository: VehicleRepository) {}

  /**
   * Adds a vehicle to the catalogue, defaulting quantity to 0 when omitted.
   *
   * @param data Vehicle fields to store.
   * @returns The created vehicle.
   */
  async addVehicle(data: Partial<CreateVehicleData> & Omit<CreateVehicleData, 'quantity'>): Promise<Vehicle> {
    return this.vehicleRepository.create({ ...data, quantity: data.quantity ?? 0 });
  }

  /**
   * Lists every vehicle, including out-of-stock ones.
   *
   * @returns All vehicles.
   */
  async listVehicles(): Promise<Vehicle[]> {
    return this.vehicleRepository.findAll();
  }

  /**
   * Searches vehicles by optional filters.
   *
   * @param filters Optional make, model, category and inclusive price range.
   * @returns Matching vehicles.
   * @throws {AppError} 400 when minPrice is greater than maxPrice.
   */
  async searchVehicles(filters: VehicleSearchFilters): Promise<Vehicle[]> {
    const { minPrice, maxPrice } = filters;
    if (minPrice !== undefined && maxPrice !== undefined && minPrice > maxPrice) {
      throw new AppError(400, 'minPrice cannot be greater than maxPrice');
    }

    return this.vehicleRepository.search(filters);
  }

  /**
   * Updates an existing vehicle.
   *
   * @param id Vehicle identifier.
   * @param data Fields to change.
   * @returns The updated vehicle.
   * @throws {AppError} 404 when the vehicle does not exist.
   */
  async updateVehicle(id: number, data: UpdateVehicleData): Promise<Vehicle> {
    await this.ensureVehicleExists(id);
    return this.vehicleRepository.update(id, data);
  }

  /**
   * Deletes an existing vehicle.
   *
   * @param id Vehicle identifier.
   * @throws {AppError} 404 when the vehicle does not exist.
   */
  async deleteVehicle(id: number): Promise<void> {
    await this.ensureVehicleExists(id);
    await this.vehicleRepository.delete(id);
  }

  /**
   * Purchases one unit, decrementing stock atomically.
   *
   * @param id Vehicle identifier.
   * @returns The vehicle with its updated stock.
   * @throws {AppError} 404 when the vehicle does not exist, 409 when out of stock.
   */
  async purchaseVehicle(id: number): Promise<Vehicle> {
    const updated = await this.vehicleRepository.decrementStockIfAvailable(id);
    if (updated) {
      return updated;
    }

    const existing = await this.vehicleRepository.findById(id);
    if (!existing) {
      throw new AppError(404, VEHICLE_NOT_FOUND_MESSAGE);
    }

    throw new AppError(409, OUT_OF_STOCK_MESSAGE);
  }

  /**
   * Restocks a vehicle by a positive amount.
   *
   * @param id Vehicle identifier.
   * @param amount Positive number of units to add.
   * @returns The vehicle with its updated stock.
   * @throws {AppError} 400 for a non-positive amount, 404 when the vehicle does not exist.
   */
  async restockVehicle(id: number, amount: number): Promise<Vehicle> {
    if (!Number.isInteger(amount) || amount <= 0) {
      throw new AppError(400, 'Restock amount must be a positive integer');
    }

    await this.ensureVehicleExists(id);
    return this.vehicleRepository.increaseStock(id, amount);
  }

  /**
   * Ensures a vehicle exists.
   *
   * @param id Vehicle identifier.
   * @throws {AppError} 404 when the vehicle does not exist.
   */
  private async ensureVehicleExists(id: number): Promise<void> {
    const vehicle = await this.vehicleRepository.findById(id);
    if (!vehicle) {
      throw new AppError(404, VEHICLE_NOT_FOUND_MESSAGE);
    }
  }
}

export default VehicleService;

Content: import type { NextFunction, Request, Response } from 'express';
import type { VehicleService } from '../services/vehicleService';
import {
  createVehicleSchema,
  restockVehicleSchema,
  searchVehiclesQuerySchema,
  updateVehicleSchema,
  vehicleIdParamSchema,
} from '../utils/validation';

/**
 * Thin HTTP layer for vehicles.
 * Parses input, delegates to the service and shapes the response.
 */
export class VehicleController {
  constructor(private readonly vehicleService: VehicleService) {}

  /**
   * Handles POST /api/vehicles.
   * Responds 201 with the created vehicle.
   */
  create = async (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): Promise<void> => {
    try {
      const data = createVehicleSchema.parse(req.body);
      const vehicle = await this.vehicleService.addVehicle(data);
      res.status(201).json(vehicle);
    } catch (error) {
      next(error);
    }
  };

  /**
   * Handles GET /api/vehicles.
   * Responds 200 with every vehicle.
   */
  list = async (_req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): Promise<void> => {
    try {
      const vehicles = await this.vehicleService.listVehicles();
      res.status(200).json(vehicles);
    } catch (error) {
      next(error);
    }
  };

  /**
   * Handles GET /api/vehicles/search.
   * Responds 200 with the matching vehicles.
   */
  search = async (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): Promise<void> => {
    try {
      const filters = searchVehiclesQuerySchema.parse(req.query);
      const vehicles = await this.vehicleService.searchVehicles(filters);
      res.status(200).json(vehicles);
    } catch (error) {
      next(error);
    }
  };

  /**
   * Handles PUT /api/vehicles/:id.
   * Responds 200 with the updated vehicle.
   */
  update = async (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): Promise<void> => {
    try {
      const { id } = vehicleIdParamSchema.parse(req.params);
      const data = updateVehicleSchema.parse(req.body);
      const vehicle = await this.vehicleService.updateVehicle(id, data);
      res.status(200).json(vehicle);
    } catch (error) {
      next(error);
    }
  };

  /**
   * Handles DELETE /api/vehicles/:id.
   * Responds 204 with no body.
   */
  remove = async (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): Promise<void> => {
    try {
      const { id } = vehicleIdParamSchema.parse(req.params);
      await this.vehicleService.deleteVehicle(id);
      res.status(204).send();
    } catch (error) {
      next(error);
    }
  };

  /**
   * Handles POST /api/vehicles/:id/purchase.
   * Responds 200 with the vehicle after its stock is decremented.
   */
  purchase = async (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): Promise<void> => {
    try {
      const { id } = vehicleIdParamSchema.parse(req.params);
      const vehicle = await this.vehicleService.purchaseVehicle(id);
      res.status(200).json(vehicle);
    } catch (error) {
      next(error);
    }
  };

  /**
   * Handles POST /api/vehicles/:id/restock.
   * Responds 200 with the vehicle after its stock is increased.
   */
  restock = async (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): Promise<void> => {
    try {
      const { id } = vehicleIdParamSchema.parse(req.params);
      const { quantity } = restockVehicleSchema.parse(req.body);
      const vehicle = await this.vehicleService.restockVehicle(id, quantity);
      res.status(200).json(vehicle);
    } catch (error) {
      next(error);
    }
  };
}

export default VehicleController;

Path: backend/src/routes/vehicleRoutes.ts
Content: import { Router } from 'express';
import { VehicleController } from '../controllers/vehicleController';
import { authenticate } from '../middleware/authenticate';
import { requireRole } from '../middleware/requireRole';
import { VehicleRepository } from '../repositories/vehicleRepository';
import { VehicleService } from '../services/vehicleService';

const ADMIN = 'ADMIN';

/**
 * Builds the vehicle router with its dependency graph wired up.
 * Every route requires authentication; mutations require the ADMIN role.
 */
export function createVehicleRouter(): Router {
  const router = Router();
  const controller = new VehicleController(new VehicleService(new VehicleRepository()));

  router.use(authenticate);

  // Registered before /:id so the literal path is not shadowed.
  router.get('/search', controller.search);

  router.get('/', controller.list);
  router.post('/', requireRole(ADMIN), controller.create);
  router.put('/:id', requireRole(ADMIN), controller.update);
  router.delete('/:id', requireRole(ADMIN), controller.remove);
  router.post('/:id/purchase', controller.purchase);
  router.post('/:id/restock', requireRole(ADMIN), controller.restock);

  return router;
}

export default createVehicleRouter;

Result: TDD GREEN phase complete. All 83 tests pass, the build compiles, and lint is clean. No test files were modified.

## Files created / changed

- [`backend/src/repositories/vehicleRepository.ts`](backend/src/repositories/vehicleRepository.ts) — `VehicleRepository` with `create`, `findAll`, `findById`, `search`, `update`, `delete`, `decrementStockIfAvailable`, `increaseStock`, all on the shared Prisma client.
  - [`decrementStockIfAvailable()`](backend/src/repositories/vehicleRepository.ts:104) is a single atomic `updateMany({ where: { id, quantity: { gt: 0 } }, data: { quantity: { decrement: 1 } } })`; returns `null` when `count === 0`, otherwise re-reads the row. No read-then-write.
  - [`search()`](backend/src/repositories/vehicleRepository.ts:66) uses `contains` for make/model (no `mode: 'insensitive'`), inclusive `gte`/`lte` for price, and filters category case-insensitively in memory via [`filterByCategory()`](backend/src/repositories/vehicleRepository.ts:139).
- [`backend/src/services/vehicleService.ts`](backend/src/services/vehicleService.ts) — `VehicleService(vehicleRepository)` with `addVehicle` (quantity defaults to 0), `listVehicles`, `searchVehicles` (400 when `minPrice > maxPrice`), `updateVehicle`/`deleteVehicle` (404), `purchaseVehicle` (404 missing, 409 `"Out of stock"`), `restockVehicle` (400 non-positive/non-integer, 404 missing).
- [`backend/src/utils/validation.ts`](backend/src/utils/validation.ts) — added `createVehicleSchema`, `updateVehicleSchema` (at least one field), `searchVehiclesQuerySchema` (coerced numeric prices, rejects non-numeric), `restockVehicleSchema` (positive integer), `vehicleIdParamSchema` (positive integer).
- [`backend/src/controllers/vehicleController.ts`](backend/src/controllers/vehicleController.ts) — thin handlers; DELETE responds `204` with no body; all errors forwarded to the existing `{ error: { message } }` handler.
- [`backend/src/routes/vehicleRoutes.ts`](backend/src/routes/vehicleRoutes.ts) — `VehicleRepository -> VehicleService -> VehicleController`; `authenticate` on all routes; `requireRole('ADMIN')` on POST `/`, PUT `/:id`, DELETE `/:id`, POST `/:id/restock`; `GET /search` registered before `/:id`.
- [`backend/src/app.ts`](backend/src/app.ts:21) — mounted at `/api/vehicles`.

<user_message>
Add a database seed script to the backend. Do not modify any existing test or any file under /backend/tests.

1. Create backend/prisma/seed.ts and add the npm script "seed": "ts-node prisma/seed.ts" to backend/package.json.
2. The script must be idempotent (safe to run many times):
   - Upsert an ADMIN user. Email from env ADMIN_EMAIL (default "admin@dealership.com"), password from env ADMIN_PASSWORD (default "Admin@12345"). Hash with bcrypt using the same cost as the auth service. If the user exists, keep its role ADMIN.
   - Upsert a regular USER with email "user@dealership.com" and password "User@12345".
   - If the Vehicle table is empty, insert 12 varied sample vehicles across categories (Sedan, SUV, Hatchback, Truck, Coupe, Electric) with realistic makes, models and prices, and quantities between 0 and 12 (at least two with quantity 0, so out-of-stock behaviour is visible).
3. Use the shared Prisma client conventions, disconnect the client at the end, and print a short summary of what was created.
4. Document ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD in backend/.env.example.

Verify: run "npm run migrate" then "npm run seed" twice (the second run must create nothing new), then run npm test, npm run build and npm run lint and show me the results. Do not leave any dev server running. Do not run git commit.

Path: backend/prisma/seed.ts
Content: import 'dotenv/config';
import bcrypt from 'bcrypt';
import { prisma } from '../src/config/prisma';

/** Bcrypt cost factor, kept in sync with the auth service. */
const BCRYPT_ROUNDS = 10;

const DEFAULT_ADMIN_EMAIL = 'admin@dealership.com';
const DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD = 'Admin@12345';
const REGULAR_USER_EMAIL = 'user@dealership.com';
const REGULAR_USER_PASSWORD = 'User@12345';

/** Sample vehicle used to populate an empty inventory. */
interface SampleVehicle {
  make: string;
  model: string;
  category: string;
  price: number;
  quantity: number;
}

/** Twelve varied vehicles across all supported categories. */
const SAMPLE_VEHICLES: SampleVehicle[] = [
  { make: 'Toyota', model: 'Camry', category: 'Sedan', price: 28500, quantity: 8 },
  { make: 'Honda', model: 'Accord', category: 'Sedan', price: 27500, quantity: 0 },
  { make: 'Ford', model: 'Explorer', category: 'SUV', price: 42000, quantity: 5 },
  { make: 'Jeep', model: 'Grand Cherokee', category: 'SUV', price: 45500, quantity: 3 },
  { make: 'Volkswagen', model: 'Golf', category: 'Hatchback', price: 22000, quantity: 12 },
  { make: 'Hyundai', model: 'i20', category: 'Hatchback', price: 18500, quantity: 0 },
  { make: 'Ford', model: 'F-150', category: 'Truck', price: 52000, quantity: 4 },
  { make: 'Chevrolet', model: 'Silverado', category: 'Truck', price: 49500, quantity: 2 },
  { make: 'Mazda', model: 'MX-5 Miata', category: 'Coupe', price: 31000, quantity: 6 },
  { make: 'BMW', model: 'M4', category: 'Coupe', price: 78000, quantity: 1 },
  { make: 'Tesla', model: 'Model 3', category: 'Electric', price: 41000, quantity: 9 },
  { make: 'Nissan', model: 'Leaf', category: 'Electric', price: 29500, quantity: 7 },
];

/**
 * Creates or updates a user, always enforcing the given role.
 *
 * @param email Unique email address.
 * @param password Plaintext password to hash.
 * @param role Role to assign (e.g. ADMIN or USER).
 * @returns Whether the user was newly created.
 */
async function upsertUser(email: string, password: string, role: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const existing = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } });
  const passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash(password, BCRYPT_ROUNDS);

  await prisma.user.upsert({
    where: { email },
    update: { passwordHash, role },
    create: { email, passwordHash, role },
  });

  return existing === null;
}

/**
 * Inserts the sample vehicles only when the inventory is empty.
 *
 * @returns The number of vehicles inserted.
 */
async function seedVehicles(): Promise<number> {
  const existingCount = await prisma.vehicle.count();
  if (existingCount > 0) {
    return 0;
  }

  await prisma.vehicle.createMany({ data: SAMPLE_VEHICLES });
  return SAMPLE_VEHICLES.length;
}

/** Runs the seed and prints a short summary. */
async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const adminEmail = process.env.ADMIN_EMAIL ?? DEFAULT_ADMIN_EMAIL;
  const adminPassword = process.env.ADMIN_PASSWORD ?? DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD;

  const adminCreated = await upsertUser(adminEmail, adminPassword, 'ADMIN');
  const userCreated = await upsertUser(REGULAR_USER_EMAIL, REGULAR_USER_PASSWORD, 'USER');
  const vehiclesCreated = await seedVehicles();

  console.log('Seed complete:');
  console.log(`  Admin user (${adminEmail}): ${adminCreated ? 'created' : 'updated'}`);
  console.log(`  Regular user (${REGULAR_USER_EMAIL}): ${userCreated ? 'created' : 'updated'}`);
  console.log(
    vehiclesCreated > 0
      ? `  Vehicles: inserted ${vehiclesCreated} sample records`
      : '  Vehicles: skipped (inventory already populated)',
  );
}

main()
  .catch((error: unknown) => {
    console.error('Seed failed:', error);
    process.exitCode = 1;
  })
  .finally(async () => {
    await prisma.$disconnect();
  });

## Changes

1. **New file [`backend/prisma/seed.ts`](backend/prisma/seed.ts)**
   - Loads env via `dotenv/config`, reuses the shared client from [`prisma`](backend/src/config/prisma.ts:7), and disconnects in a `finally` block.
   - `upsertUser()` uses `prisma.user.upsert` keyed on `email`, hashing with bcrypt at cost `10` (same as [`BCRYPT_ROUNDS`](backend/src/services/authService.ts:6)). On update it re-applies the role, so an existing admin is always kept as `ADMIN`.
   - Admin: `ADMIN_EMAIL` (default `admin@dealership.com`) / `ADMIN_PASSWORD` (default `Admin@12345`), role `ADMIN`.
   - Regular user: `user@dealership.com` / `User@12345`, role `USER`.
   - `seedVehicles()` only inserts when `prisma.vehicle.count() === 0`, adding 12 vehicles across Sedan, SUV, Hatchback, Truck, Coupe and Electric, with quantities 0–12 (two at 0: Honda Accord, Hyundai i20).
   - Prints a summary of created/updated users and inserted/skipped vehicles; sets a non-zero exit code on failure.

Build in a test-first way: for each unit below, write its tests first, run them to see them fail, then implement until they pass.

1. src/types.ts: User { id, email, role }, Vehicle { id, make, model, category, price, quantity }.
2. src/api/client.ts: a small fetch wrapper. Base URL from import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL (default http://localhost:4000). Attaches "Authorization: Bearer <token>" when a token exists. Throws an Error carrying the server's error.message on non-2xx responses (the backend returns { error: { message } }). Handles 204 with no body. Export typed functions: register(email, password), login(email, password).
3. src/context/AuthContext.tsx: AuthProvider and useAuth() exposing user, token, isAdmin, login, register, logout. Persist token and user in localStorage (wrap in try/catch). Registering does NOT log the user in: after register the page sends them to the login page.
4. src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx: redirects to /login when there is no token. Optional adminOnly prop that redirects non-admins to /.
5. src/components/Navbar.tsx: app name, shows the user's email and a logout button when logged in, links to login/register otherwise. Responsive.
6. src/pages/LoginPage.tsx and RegisterPage.tsx: clean, centered cards styled with Tailwind, labelled inputs, client-side validation (valid email, password at least 8 characters), inline error messages, loading state on the submit button, server error displayed. Register page confirms password.
7. src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx: placeholder that says "Vehicles coming soon" (the real dashboard is a later task), wrapped in ProtectedRoute.
8. src/App.tsx with routes: /login, /register, / (dashboard, protected), * redirects to /.

Tests (Vitest + RTL, mock the api module with vi.mock, no real network): AuthContext (login stores token and user, logout clears them, isAdmin), ProtectedRoute (redirect and render cases, adminOnly), LoginPage and RegisterPage (validation messages, successful submit calls the API, server error shown).

Design: modern and clean, a neutral slate palette with one accent color, readable typography, mobile-first. Keep it simple, no extra libraries beyond those listed. Add a frontend/.env.example with VITE_API_URL.

 3 | import { AppError } from '../utils/AppError';
 4 | 
 5 | const GENERIC_MESSAGE = 'Internal Server Error';
 6 | 
 7 | /** Builds a Zod error message from the first issue, prefixed by its field path. */
 8 | function formatZodError(error: ZodError): string {
 9 |   const issue = error.issues[0];
10 |   if (!issue) {
11 |     return 'Invalid request payload';
12 |   }
13 |   const field = issue.path.join('.');
14 |   return field ? `${field}: ${issue.message}` : issue.message;
15 | }
16 | 
17 | /**
18 |  * Central error-handling middleware.
19 |  * Every response is JSON shaped as `{ error: { message } }`.
20 |  * Must be registered last, after all routes.
21 |  */
22 | export function errorHandler(
23 |   err: unknown,
24 |   _req: Request,
25 |   res: Response,
26 |   _next: NextFunction,
27 | ): void {
28 |   if (err instanceof AppError) {
29 |     res.status(err.statusCode).json({ error: { message: err.message } });
30 |     return;
31 |   }
32 | 
33 |   if (err instanceof ZodError) {
34 |     res.status(400).json({ error: { message: formatZodError(err) } });
35 |     return;
36 |   }
37 | 
38 |   res.status(500).json({ error: { message: GENERIC_MESSAGE } });
39 | }

23 | /**
24 |  * Authentication business logic: registration and login.
25 |  * Dependencies are injected to keep the service testable and decoupled.
26 |  */
27 | export class AuthService {
28 |   constructor(private readonly userRepository: UserRepository) {}
29 | 
30 |   /**
31 |    * Registers a new user with the USER role and a hashed password.
32 |    *
33 |    * @param email Unique email address.
34 |    * @param password Plaintext password to hash.
35 |    * @returns The created user's public fields.
36 |    * @throws {AppError} 409 when the email is already registered.
37 |    */
38 |   async register(email: string, password: string): Promise<PublicUser> {
39 |     const existing = await this.userRepository.findByEmail(email);
40 |     if (existing) {
41 |       throw new AppError(409, 'Email is already registered');
42 |     }
43 | 
44 |     const passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash(password, BCRYPT_ROUNDS);
45 |     const user = await this.userRepository.create({
46 |       email,
47 |       passwordHash,
48 |       role: DEFAULT_ROLE,
49 |     });
50 | 
51 |     return this.toPublicUser(user);
52 |   }
53 | 
54 |   /**
55 |    * Authenticates a user and issues a signed JWT.
56 |    *
57 |    * @param email Email address.
58 |    * @param password Plaintext password to verify.
59 |    * @returns A signed token and the user's public fields.
60 |    * @throws {AppError} 401 for an unknown email or a wrong password.
61 |    */
62 |   async login(email: string, password: string): Promise<LoginResult> {
63 |     const user = await this.userRepository.findByEmail(email);
64 |     if (!user) {
65 |       throw new AppError(401, INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MESSAGE);
66 |     }
67 | 
68 |     const passwordMatches = await bcrypt.compare(password, user.passwordHash);
69 |     if (!passwordMatches) {
70 |       throw new AppError(401, INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MESSAGE);
71 |     }
72 | 
73 |     return { token: this.signToken(user), user: this.toPublicUser(user) };
74 |   }
75 | 
76 |   /**
77 |    * Signs a JWT for the user. Env vars are read at call time so tests can set them.
78 |    */
79 |   private signToken(user: { id: number; role: string }): string {
80 |     const secret = process.env.JWT_SECRET;
81 |     if (!secret) {
82 |       throw new AppError(500, 'Authentication is not configured');
83 |     }
84 | 
85 |     const options: SignOptions = {
86 |       expiresIn: (process.env.JWT_EXPIRES_IN ?? '1d') as SignOptions['expiresIn'],
87 |     };
88 | 
89 |     return jwt.sign({ sub: String(user.id), role: user.role }, secret, options);
90 |   }
91 | 
92 |   /** Strips sensitive fields from a user record. */
93 |   private toPublicUser(user: { id: number; email: string; role: string }): PublicUser {
94 |     return { id: user.id, email: user.email, role: user.role };
95 |   }
96 | }
97 |

For the fetch wrapper design:

```ts
const DEFAULT_BASE_URL = 'http://localhost:4000';

export interface ApiErrorBody {
  error?: { message?: string };
}

function getBaseUrl(): string {
  return import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL ?? DEFAULT_BASE_URL;
}

export function getToken(): string | null {
  try {
    return localStorage.getItem('token');
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

export class ApiError extends Error {} // maybe not needed; task says "Throws an Error carrying the server's error.message"

export async function apiFetch<T>(path: string, options: RequestInit = {}): Promise<T> {
  const headers = new Headers(options.headers);
  headers.set('Content-Type', 'application/json');
  const token = getToken();
  if (token) {
    headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`);
  }
  const response = await fetch(`${getBaseUrl()}${path}`, { ...options, headers });
  if (!response.ok) {
    const body = await response.json().catch(() => null);
    const message = body?.error?.message ?? `Request failed with status ${response.status}`;
    throw new Error(message);
  }
  if (response.status === 204) {
    return undefined as T;
  }
  return response.json() as Promise<T>;
}

export function register(email: string, password: string): Promise<User> {
  return apiFetch<User>('/api/auth/register', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
  });
}

export function login(email: string, password: string): Promise<LoginResponse> {
  return apiFetch<LoginResponse>('/api/auth/login', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
  });
}
```

Let me design client.ts:

```ts
import type { User } from '../types';

const DEFAULT_BASE_URL = 'http://localhost:4000';
const TOKEN_KEY = 'token';

export interface LoginResponse {
  token: string;
  user: User;
}

function getBaseUrl(): string {
  return import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL ?? DEFAULT_BASE_URL;
}

function getToken(): string | null {
  try {
    return localStorage.getItem(TOKEN_KEY);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

async function request<T>(path: string, options: RequestInit = {}): Promise<T> {
  const headers = new Headers(options.headers);
  if (!headers.has('Content-Type') && options.body) {
    headers.set('Content-Type', 'application/json');
  }
  const token = getToken();
  if (token) {
    headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`);
  }
  const response = await fetch(`${getBaseUrl()}${path}`, { ...options, headers });
  if (response.status === 204) {
    return undefined as T;
  }
  let data: unknown = null;
  const text = await response.text();
  if (text) {
    try {
      data = JSON.parse(text);
    } catch {
      data = null;
    }
  }
  if (!response.ok) {
    const message =
      data && typeof data === 'object' && 'error' in data
        ? (data as { error?: { message?: string } }).error?.message
        : undefined;
    throw new Error(message ?? `Request failed with status ${response.status}`);
  }
  return data as T;
}

export function register(email: string, password: string): Promise<User> {
  return request<User>('/api/auth/register', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
  });
}

export function login(email: string, password: string): Promise<LoginResponse> {
  return request<LoginResponse>('/api/auth/login', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
  });
}
```

Wait, `import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL` default `http://localhost:4000`. The task says "Base URL from import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL (default http://localhost:4000)". Good.

Now AuthContext.tsx:

```tsx
import { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useMemo, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import * as api from '../api/client';
import type { User } from '../types';

const TOKEN_KEY = 'token';
const USER_KEY = 'user';

interface AuthContextValue {
  user: User | null;
  token: string | null;
  isAdmin: boolean;
  login: (email: string, password: string) => Promise<void>;
  register: (email: string, password: string) => Promise<void>;
  logout: () => void;
}

const AuthContext = createContext<AuthContextValue | undefined>(undefined);

function readToken(): string | null {
  try { return localStorage.getItem(TOKEN_KEY); } catch { return null; }
}

function readUser(): User | null {
  try {
    const raw = localStorage.getItem(USER_KEY);
    return raw ? (JSON.parse(raw) as User) : null;
  } catch { return null; }
}

export function AuthProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [token, setToken] = useState<string | null>(readToken);
  const [user, setUser] = useState<User | null>(readUser);

  const login = useCallback(async (email: string, password: string) => {
    const result = await api.login(email, password);
    setToken(result.token);
    setUser(result.user);
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(TOKEN_KEY, result.token);
      localStorage.setItem(USER_KEY, JSON.stringify(result.user));
    } catch { /* ignore */ }
  }, []);

  const register = useCallback(async (email: string, password: string) => {
    await api.register(email, password);
  }, []);

  const logout = useCallback(() => {
    setToken(null);
    setUser(null);
    try {
      localStorage.removeItem(TOKEN_KEY);
      localStorage.removeItem(USER_KEY);
    } catch { /* ignore */ }
  }, []);

  const value = useMemo<AuthContextValue>(() => ({
    user,
    token,
    isAdmin: user?.role === 'ADMIN',
    login,
    register,
    logout,
  }), [user, token, login, register, logout]);

  return <AuthContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</AuthContext.Provider>;
}

export function useAuth(): AuthContextValue {
  const ctx = useContext(AuthContext);
  if (!ctx) {
    throw new Error('useAuth must be used within an AuthProvider');
  }
  return ctx;
}
```

Note: `register` in context calls api.register but doesn't set token/user. Good. Registering does NOT log in.

The `isAdmin` check: `user?.role === 'ADMIN'`.

import { Navigate } from 'react-router-dom';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { useAuth } from '../context/AuthContext';

interface ProtectedRouteProps {
  children: ReactNode;
  adminOnly?: boolean;
}

export default function ProtectedRoute({ children, adminOnly = false }: ProtectedRouteProps) {
  const { token, isAdmin } = useAuth();
  if (!token) {
    return <Navigate to="/login" replace />;
  }
  if (adminOnly && !isAdmin) {
    return <Navigate to="/" replace />;
  }
  return <>{children}</>;
}

Requirements: clean centered card, labelled inputs, client-side validation (valid email, password ≥ 8), inline error messages, loading state on submit button, server error displayed.

Design:

```tsx
import { useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import { Link, useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom';
import { useAuth } from '../context/AuthContext';

function validate(email: string, password: string): { email?: string; password?: string } {
  const errors: { email?: string; password?: string } = {};
  if (!email) errors.email = 'Email is required';
  else if (!/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email)) errors.email = 'Enter a valid email address';
  if (!password) errors.password = 'Password is required';
  else if (password.length < 8) errors.password = 'Password must be at least 8 characters';
  return errors;
}

export default function LoginPage() {
  const { login } = useAuth();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('');
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('');
  const [fieldErrors, setFieldErrors] = useState<{email?: string; password?: string}>({});
  const [serverError, setServerError] = useState('');
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);

  const handleSubmit = async (e: FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const errors = validate(email, password);
    setFieldErrors(errors);
    if (Object.keys(errors).length > 0) return;
    setLoading(true);
    setServerError('');
    try {
      await login(email, password);
      navigate('/');
    } catch (err) {
      setServerError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Login failed');
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };

  return (...form...);
}
```

Let me finalize client request:

```ts
async function request<T>(path, options = {}) {
  const headers = new Headers(options.headers);
  if (options.body && !headers.has('Content-Type')) {
    headers.set('Content-Type', 'application/json');
  }
  const token = readToken();
  if (token) headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`);

  const response = await fetch(`${getBaseUrl()}${path}`, { ...options, headers });

  if (response.status === 204) {
    return undefined as T;
  }

  const text = await response.text();
  let data: unknown = null;
  if (text) {
    try { data = JSON.parse(text); } catch { data = null; }
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    const message = extractErrorMessage(data);
    throw new Error(message ?? `Request failed with status ${response.status}`);
  }

  return data as T;
}
```

`Headers` is available in jsdom? Yes, jsdom provides Headers. In Node, Headers is global too. Vitest jsdom env provides Headers. Good.

`extractErrorMessage`:

```ts
function extractErrorMessage(data: unknown): string | undefined {
  if (data && typeof data === 'object' && 'error' in data) {
    const error = (data as { error?: unknown }).error;
    if (error && typeof error === 'object' && 'message' in error) {
      const message = (error as { message?: unknown }).message;
      if (typeof message === 'string') return message;
    }
  }
  return undefined;
}
```

Let me write extractErrorMessage carefully:

```ts
function extractErrorMessage(data: unknown): string | undefined {
  if (typeof data !== 'object' || data === null || !('error' in data)) {
    return undefined;
  }
  const error = (data as { error?: unknown }).error;
  if (typeof error !== 'object' || error === null || !('message' in error)) {
    return undefined;
  }
  const message = (error as { message?: unknown }).message;
  return typeof message === 'string' ? message : undefined;
}
```

Actually, let me design the client API precisely:

```ts
const DEFAULT_BASE_URL = 'http://localhost:4000';
export const TOKEN_KEY = 'token';

function getBaseUrl(): string {
  return import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL ?? DEFAULT_BASE_URL;
}

function getToken(): string | null {
  try {
    return localStorage.getItem(TOKEN_KEY);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

async function request<T>(path: string, options: RequestInit = {}): Promise<T> {
  const headers = new Headers(options.headers);
  if (!headers.has('Content-Type') && options.body) {
    headers.set('Content-Type', 'application/json');
  }
  const token = getToken();
  if (token) {
    headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`);
  }
  const response = await fetch(`${getBaseUrl()}${path}`, { ...options, headers });
  if (!response.ok) {
    let message = 'Request failed';
    try {
      const body = await response.json();
      message = body?.error?.message ?? message;
    } catch {
      // ignore
    }
    throw new Error(message);
  }
  if (response.status === 204) {
    return undefined as T;
  }
  return response.json() as Promise<T>;
}

export function register(email: string, password: string): Promise<User> {
  return request<User>('/api/auth/register', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
  });
}

export function login(email: string, password: string): Promise<{ token: string; user: User }> {
  return request<{ token: string; user: User }>('/api/auth/login', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
  });
}
```

Content: import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { login, register, TOKEN_KEY } from './client';

const okResponse = (body: unknown, status = 200): Response =>
  new Response(JSON.stringify(body), {
    status,
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  });

describe('api client', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    localStorage.clear();
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn());
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
  });

  it('register posts to /api/auth/register with the payload and returns the created user', async () => {
    const user = { id: 1, email: 'a@example.com', role: 'USER' };
    vi.mocked(fetch).mockResolvedValue(okResponse(user, 201));

    const result = await register('a@example.com', 'password123');

    expect(result).toEqual(user);
    expect(fetch).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      'http://localhost:4000/api/auth/register',
      expect.objectContaining({
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({ email: 'a@example.com', password: 'password123' }),
      }),
    );
  });

  it('login posts to /api/auth/login and returns token and user', async () => {
    const payload = { token: 'jwt', user: { id: 1, email: 'a@example.com', role: 'ADMIN' } };
    vi.mocked(fetch).mockResolvedValue(okResponse(payload, 200));

    const result = await login('a@example.com', 'password123');

    expect(result).toEqual(payload);
    expect(fetch).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      'http://localhost:4000/api/auth/login',
      expect.objectContaining({ method: 'POST' }),
    );
  });

  it('attaches an Authorization bearer header when a token exists', async () => {
    localStorage.setItem(TOKEN_KEY, 'abc');
    vi.mocked(fetch).mockResolvedValue(okResponse({}));

    await login('a@example.com', 'password123');

    const [, options] = vi.mocked(fetch).mock.calls[0];
    const headers = options?.headers as Headers;
    expect(headers.get('Authorization')).toBe('Bearer abc');
  });

  it('omits the Authorization header when no token exists', async () => {
    vi.mocked(fetch).mockResolvedValue(okResponse({}));

    await login('a@example.com', 'password123');

    const [, options] = vi.mocked(fetch).mock.calls[0];
    const headers = options?.headers as Headers;
    expect(headers.has('Authorization')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('throws an Error carrying the server error message on non-2xx responses', async () => {
    vi.mocked(fetch).mockResolvedValue(
      okResponse({ error: { message: 'Invalid credentials' } }, 401),
    );

    await expect(login('a@example.com', 'wrong')).rejects.toThrow('Invalid credentials');
  });

  it('resolves without parsing a body on 204 responses', async () => {
    vi.mocked(fetch).mockResolvedValue(new Response(null, { status: 204 }));

    const result = await login('a@example.com', 'password123');

    expect(result).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

Path: frontend/src/api/client.ts
Content: import type { User } from '../types';

/** Key under which the auth token is stored in localStorage. */
export const TOKEN_KEY = 'token';

/** Base API URL, read from the environment with a sensible local default. */
const BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL ?? 'http://localhost:4000';

/** Reads the persisted token, tolerating environments without localStorage. */
function getToken(): string | null {
  try {
    return localStorage.getItem(TOKEN_KEY);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/** Parses a response body as JSON, returning undefined for empty (e.g. 204) bodies. */
async function parseBody(response: Response): Promise<unknown> {
  if (response.status === 204) {
    return undefined;
  }
  return response.json();
}

/**
 * Thin fetch wrapper around the backend API.
 * Attaches a bearer token when present and surfaces server error messages.
 *
 * @throws {Error} With the server's `error.message` when the response is not 2xx.
 */
async function request<T>(path: string, options: RequestInit = {}): Promise<T> {
  const token = getToken();
  const headers = new Headers(options.headers);
  headers.set('Content-Type', 'application/json');
  if (token) {
    headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`);
  }

  const response = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}${path}`, { ...options, headers });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const body = (await parseBody(response)) as { error?: { message?: string } } | undefined;
    throw new Error(body?.error?.message ?? `Request failed with status ${response.status}`);
  }

  return (await parseBody(response)) as T;
}

/** Result of a successful login: a signed token plus the user's public profile. */
export interface LoginResult {
  token: string;
  user: User;
}

/** Registers a new user. The backend responds 201 with the created user and no token. */
export function register(email: string, password: string): Promise<User> {
  return request<User>('/api/auth/register', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
  });
}

/** Logs a user in, returning a token and the user's public profile. */
export function login(email: string, password: string): Promise<LoginResult> {
  return request<LoginResult>('/api/auth/login', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
  });
}

Path: frontend/src/context/AuthContext.test.tsx
Content: import { render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import type { User } from '../types';
import { AuthProvider, useAuth } from './AuthContext';

vi.mock('../api/client', () => ({
  login: vi.fn(),
  register: vi.fn(),
  TOKEN_KEY: 'token',
}));

import { login, register } from '../api/client';

const USER_KEY = 'user';

/** Minimal consumer exposing the auth context for assertions. */
function Consumer() {
  const { user, token, isAdmin, login, register, logout } = useAuth();
  return (
    <div>
      <span data-testid="token">{token ?? 'none'}</span>
      <span data-testid="user">{user?.email ?? 'none'}</span>
      <span data-testid="isAdmin">{String(isAdmin)}</span>
      <button onClick={() => login('a@example.com', 'password123')}>login</button>
      <button onClick={() => register('a@example.com', 'password123')}>register</button>
      <button onClick={logout}>logout</button>
    </div>
  );
}

function renderWithProvider() {
  return render(
    <AuthProvider>
      <Consumer />
    </AuthProvider>,
  );
}

const user: User = { id: 1, email: 'a@example.com', role: 'ADMIN' };

describe('AuthContext', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    localStorage.clear();
    vi.mocked(login).mockReset();
    vi.mocked(register).mockReset();
  });

  it('starts with no token and no user', () => {
    renderWithProvider();
    expect(screen.getByTestId('token')).toHaveTextContent('none');
    expect(screen.getByTestId('user')).toHaveTextContent('none');
    expect(screen.getByTestId('isAdmin')).toHaveTextContent('false');
  });

  it('login stores the token and user in state and localStorage', async () => {
    vi.mocked(login).mockResolvedValue({ token: 'jwt-token', user });

    renderWithProvider();
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'login' }));

    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(screen.getByTestId('token')).toHaveTextContent('jwt-token');
      expect(screen.getByTestId('user')).toHaveTextContent('a@example.com');
    });
    expect(localStorage.getItem('token')).toBe('jwt-token');
    expect(JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(USER_KEY)!)).toEqual(user);
  });

  it('logout clears token and user from state and localStorage', async () => {
    vi.mocked(login).mockResolvedValue({ token: 'jwt-token', user });
    renderWithProvider();
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'login' }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId('token')).toHaveTextContent('jwt-token'));

    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'logout' }));

    expect(screen.getByTestId('token')).toHaveTextContent('none');
    expect(screen.getByTestId('user')).toHaveTextContent('none');
    expect(localStorage.getItem('token')).toBeNull();
    expect(localStorage.getItem(USER_KEY)).toBeNull();
  });

  it('isAdmin is true only for ADMIN role users', async () => {
    vi.mocked(login).mockResolvedValue({ token: 'jwt-token', user });

    renderWithProvider();
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'login' }));

    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId('isAdmin')).toHaveTextContent('true'));
  });

  it('register calls the API but does not log the user in', async () => {
    vi.mocked(register).mockResolvedValue({ id: 2, email: 'b@example.com', role: 'USER' });

    renderWithProvider();
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'register' }));

    await waitFor(() => expect(register).toHaveBeenCalledWith('a@example.com', 'password123'));
    expect(screen.getByTestId('token')).toHaveTextContent('none');
    expect(screen.getByTestId('user')).toHaveTextContent('none');
  });
});

Path: frontend/src/context/AuthContext.tsx
Content: import {
  createContext,
  useCallback,
  useContext,
  useMemo,
  useState,
  type ReactNode,
} from 'react';
import { login as apiLogin, register as apiRegister, TOKEN_KEY } from '../api/client';
import type { User } from '../types';

const USER_KEY = 'user';

/** Shape exposed to consumers via useAuth(). */
interface AuthContextValue {
  user: User | null;
  token: string | null;
  isAdmin: boolean;
  login: (email: string, password: string) => Promise<void>;
  register: (email: string, password) => Promise<void>;
  logout: () => void;
}

const AuthContext = createContext<AuthContextValue | undefined>(undefined);

/** Safely reads persisted JSON from localStorage, returning null on any failure. */
function readPersistedUser(): User | null {
  try {
    const raw = localStorage.getItem(USER_KEY);
    return raw ? (JSON.parse(raw) as User) : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/** Safely reads the persisted token from localStorage, returning null on any failure. */
function readPersistedToken(): string | null {
  try {
    return localStorage.getItem(TOKEN_KEY);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/**
 * Provides authentication state to the app.
 * Persists token and user in localStorage, wrapped in try/catch for safety.
 */
export function AuthProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [token, setToken] = useState<string | null>(() => readPersistedToken());
  const [user, setUser] = useState<User | null>(() => readPersistedUser());

  const login = useCallback(async (email: string, password: string) => {
    const result = await apiLogin(email, password);
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(TOKEN_KEY, result.token);
      localStorage.setItem(USER_KEY, JSON.stringify(result.user));
    } catch {
      // Persistence is best-effort; the in-memory session still works.
    }
    setToken(result.token);
    setUser(result.user);
  }, []);

  const register = useCallback(async (email: string, password: string) => {
    // Registration does not create a session; the caller redirects to /login.
    await apiRegister(email, password);
  }, []);

  const logout = useCallback(() => {
    try {
      localStorage.removeItem(TOKEN_KEY);
      localStorage.removeItem(USER_KEY);
    } catch {
      // Ignore storage failures during logout.
    }
    setToken(null);
    setUser(null);
  }, []);

  const value = useMemo<AuthContextValue>(
    () => ({
      user,
      token,
      isAdmin: user?.role === 'ADMIN',
      login,
      register,
      logout,
    }),
    [user, token, login, register, logout],
  );

  return <AuthContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</AuthContext.Provider>;
}

/** Hook to access authentication state; must be used within an AuthProvider. */
export function useAuth(): AuthContextValue {
  const context = useContext(AuthContext);
  if (!context) {
    throw new Error('useAuth must be used within an AuthProvider');
  }
  return context;
}

Content: import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import { MemoryRouter, Route, Routes } from 'react-router-dom';
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import type { User } from '../types';
import ProtectedRoute from './ProtectedRoute';

vi.mock('../context/AuthContext', () => ({
  useAuth: vi.fn(),
}));

import { useAuth } from '../context/AuthContext';

const mockUseAuth = vi.mocked(useAuth);

/** Renders the route under test with a public /login route to capture redirects. */
function renderRoute({ adminOnly = false }: { adminOnly?: boolean } = {}) {
  return render(
    <MemoryRouter initialEntries={['/']}>
      <Routes>
        <Route path="/login" element={<div>Login page</div>} />
        <Route path="/" element={<div>Home page</div>} />
        <Route
          path="/protected"
          element={
            <ProtectedRoute adminOnly={adminOnly}>
              <div>Protected content</div>
            </ProtectedRoute>
          }
        />
      </Routes>
    </MemoryRouter>,
  );
}

function setAuth(token: string | null, user: User | null) {
  mockUseAuth.mockReturnValue({
    user,
    token,
    isAdmin: user?.role === 'ADMIN',
    login: vi.fn(),
    register: vi.fn(),
    logout: vi.fn(),
  });
}

describe('ProtectedRoute', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    mockUseAuth.mockReset();
  });

  it('renders children when a token is present', () => {
    setAuth('jwt', { id: 1, email: 'a@example.com', role: 'USER' });

    renderRoute();

    expect(screen.getByText('Protected content')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('redirects to /login when there is no token', () => {
    setAuth(null, null);

    renderRoute();

    expect(screen.getByText('Login page')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByText('Protected content')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('renders children for admins when adminOnly is set', () => {
    setAuth('jwt', { id: 1, email: 'a@example.com', role: 'ADMIN' });

    renderRoute({ adminOnly: true });

    expect(screen.getByText('Protected content')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('redirects non-admin users to / when adminOnly is set', () => {
    setAuth('jwt', { id: 1, email: 'a@example.com', role: 'USER' });

    renderRoute({ adminOnly: true });

    expect(screen.getByText('Home page')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByText('Protected content')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});

Path: frontend/src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx
Content: import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { Navigate } from 'react-router-dom';
import { useAuth } from '../context/AuthContext';

interface ProtectedRouteProps {
  children: ReactNode;
  adminOnly?: boolean;
}

/**
 * Guards a route so only authenticated (and optionally admin) users can view it.
 * Redirects to /login when unauthenticated and to / when not an admin.
 */
export default function ProtectedRoute({ children, adminOnly = false }: ProtectedRouteProps) {
  const { token, isAdmin } = useAuth();

  if (!token) {
    return <Navigate to="/login" replace />;
  }

  if (adminOnly && !isAdmin) {
    return <Navigate to="/" replace />;
  }

  return <>{children}</>;
}

Path: frontend/src/components/Navbar.test.tsx
Content: import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import type { User } from '../types';
import Navbar from './Navbar';

vi.mock('../context/AuthContext', () => ({
  useAuth: vi.fn(),
}));

import { useAuth } from '../context/AuthContext';

const mockUseAuth = vi.mocked(useAuth);

const logout = vi.fn();

function setAuth(token: string | null, user: User | null) {
  mockUseAuth.mockReturnValue({
    user,
    token,
    isAdmin: user?.role === 'ADMIN',
    login: vi.fn(),
    register: vi.fn(),
    logout,
  });
}

describe('Navbar', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    mockUseAuth.mockReset();
    logout.mockReset();
  });

  it('shows the app name', () => {
    setAuth(null, null);
    render(
      <MemoryRouter>
        <Navbar />
      </MemoryRouter>,
    );

    expect(screen.getByText('Car Dealership')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('shows the user email and a logout button when logged in', async () => {
    setAuth('jwt', { id: 1, email: 'a@example.com', role: 'USER' });
    render(
      <MemoryRouter>
        <Navbar />
      </MemoryRouter>,
    );

    expect(screen.getByText('a@example.com')).toBeInTheDocument();
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Logout' }));
    expect(logout).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it('shows login and register links when logged out', () => {
    setAuth(null, null);
    render(
      <MemoryRouter>
        <Navbar />
      </MemoryRouter>,
    );

    expect(screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Login' })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Register' })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByRole('button', { name: 'Logout' })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
